chapter: The word jazz and the band's New York success
title: How the word spread, and Japan's 1919 jazz club
summary: He says records, not the word, spread jazz worldwide, noting a jazz club in Japan in 1919 and New Orleans only in 1949.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: No, not that fast. Yeah. No, it didn't caught on that fast. It was the records that had worldwide distribution that went as far as Honolulu, Germany, Japan. If you look up my clippings, you'll find they had a jazz club in Japan in 1919. Look, they only got a jazz club in New Orleans in 1949. That's funny, ain't it? 30 years after Japan has a jazz club. They built a New Orleans jazz club. And this man becomes a historian.

Now, one of the things that I'm personally interested in is the way the public, or certain aspects of the public, the way the press, or certain aspects of the press, opposed jazz in the beginning. They thought it was not something that ought to be encouraged.
Now, would you care to comment on the whole history of the way jazz finally got to be adopted?
